question: is each money leg's sigma made of the bars it is meant to judge, and does an extreme bar come back as a quote flip, a re-accrual, or not at all?

ruler.sigma_plain: sample std of daily returns in bp (r2048's ruler, re-derived)
ruler.bars_to_half: first k with |px[t+k]/px[t-1]-1| <= 0.5 x |move|, up to 750 bars

shapes.OFF_PACE: comes back, but not on the accrual clock (faster = a second print did it)

ruler.accrual_predicted_half: |move| / (2 x median daily return) -- the half-time a payout must show
ruler.fake_left_bp_yr: sum of the 3 bars after each SNAP bar the zero rule keeps, in bp of level per year
ruler.deleted_bp_yr: sum of |move| for NEVER bars the zero rule erases, bp of level per year
ruler.annualisation: cash_shelf_year_by_year.bars_per_year on the instrument's own bars
ruler.this_is_not: a return estimate and not a significance test

contamination.rule: median daily return >= 2 bp (equity speed) inside a class the census calls money
contamination.name_match: 现金流 (cash-flow factor) read as 现金 (cash): 20 of 20 excluded names contain it
contamination.why_it_matters: a 现金流 equity ETF accrues 4-16 bp a day; mixed into a money shelf it moves every shelf-wide median, including the two that r2046/r2048 print

not_claimed: BARS_TO_HALF describes the path; it does not say why the price moved.
NEVER means 'not inside the 750-bar walk', not 'never' in the world.
For a share-paying vehicle the close is not a return: its two bp/yr columns are a level convention, not a return, and they are printed only where a clock exists.
The contamination split uses a mechanical accrual-speed rule; the class map itself is upstream and is not edited here.
